mainTopic: ביטול ברוב and the טומאה of a ולד, the skein measures for a fetus's head, and purifying brine from an עם הארץ
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: the lump of blood is buried so people know the mother animal is now free from בכורה. The גמרא then asks why a real ולד like this gives no טומאה. רבי יוחנן answers that it is cancelled by the bigger mass around it (ביטול ברוב). He links this to רבי שמעון, who says a ולד inside a שליא dissolved before it came out. Next, a משנה teaches that a dead fetus gives טומאה only once its head is round like a פיקה (skein). The גמרא works out which skein is meant: a warp skein for a woman's fetus, a woof skein for an animal's fetus, and a large sack-makers' skein for an impure clod of earth. Then ריש לקיש rules that brine bought from an עם הארץ becomes טהור by touching it to מקוה water. רבי ירמיה limits this to dipping bread, because in a pot the cancelled water 'wakes up'. אביי questions whether cancelled טומאה can return, and רב דימי begins a proof from a משנה about impure תרומה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: It is buried so everyone knows the mother is free from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The lump is buried to make it public that the mother animal is now free from the law of בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is buried in order to publicize that she is exempt from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering why the lump of blood must be buried. Burying it makes people aware that the mother animal is now exempt from בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial is not done because the lump is holy or impure. It is a public sign. Once people know this mother already gave birth, they will not treat her next offspring as a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: to make it public about her (the mother animal)
she became exempt
the law of the firstborn animal

phrases.english: In order to publicize about her
phrases.notes: "Her" is the mother animal, so people will know about her next birth.

phrases.english: that she is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section about why the lump must be buried.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Burial publicizes that the mother is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: If it is a real offspring, why is it not impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the lump counts as a full ולד. It then asks why it gives no טומאה by touching or carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is to say that it is a full-fledged offspring. But then why does it not make things impure, either by touching or by carrying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that if the lump frees the mother from בכורה, it must be a real ולד. It then challenges: a real dead ולד should give off טומאה, so why doesn't this one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rulings seem to clash. For בכורה the lump is treated as a real birth. For טומאה it is treated as nothing. The גמרא wants to know how one object can be a full ולד in one area and not in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: is this to say? (drawing a conclusion)
a full, proper offspring
טומאה passed on by touching
טומאה passed on by carrying

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the lump stops being a ולד. It is a real ולד, and the question is only why the usual טומאה rule does not apply to it.

phrases.english: That is to say it is a full-fledged offspring,
so why does it not make things impure
neither by touching nor by carrying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the exemption from בכורה to show the lump is a real ולד, then attacks the ruling of no טומאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the lump gives no טומאה by touching or carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something real enough to exempt from בכורה should be real enough to carry the טומאה of a dead ולד.

steps.title: The ולד is cancelled by the larger mass of blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the חכמים removed the טומאה because of ביטול ברוב: the ולד is lost inside the larger mass.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because of nullification in a majority, they dealt with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The ולד is real, but it is mixed into a bigger mass of blood, so it is cancelled for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בכורה, what counts is that a birth took place, and that cannot be undone. For touching and carrying, what counts is the object in your hand, which is mostly blood. The small ולד is cancelled by the majority, so the mass gives no טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: something being cancelled because a larger amount surrounds it
they dealt with it (the חכמים ruled about it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the same lump can count for בכורה and not for טומאה. The category of ולד stays, but טומאה is not applied in this case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Because of nullification in a majority they dealt with it.
phrases.notes: Literally "they touched it." He means the חכמים took up this case and removed its טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל בְּרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two laws: the birth counts for בכורה, while ביטול ברוב cancels the ולד for טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A real ולד should always give off טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ולד is real, but it is cancelled by the bigger mass of blood, so it does not give off טומאה by touching or carrying.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן links רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows this answer matches רבי יוחנן's other teaching, that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, for רבי יוחנן said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון said the same thing. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן's answer fits another teaching of his, that two תנאים share the same idea. It sets up the next move, which will show what רבי שמעון said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (our lump of blood) and רבי שמעון both rely on the ולד being cancelled or lost. The view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב was already given, so only רבי שמעון's view still needs to be shown.

keyTerms.meaning: he goes according to his own reasoning
one and the same idea
this that we said

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon
said the same thing,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov — that which we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to our משנה's case of the lump of blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוחנן's answer in step 3 matches another of his statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן says רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון rely on the same principle.

steps.title: What did רבי שמעון say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי שמעון רבי יוחנן meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the statement of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון taught this idea. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view was already known from our משנה. To prove the two views match, the גמרא needs the source for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon — what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second half of the link made in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source where רבי שמעון taught the same principle.

steps.title: The משנה of the שליא in a house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a שליא in a house makes the house impure because a שליא always has a ולד in it. רבי שמעון says the ולד dissolved before it came out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If the afterbirth is in the house, the house is impure. Not because the afterbirth is an offspring, but because there is no afterbirth without an offspring. רבי שמעון says: The offspring dissolved before it came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that holds רבי שמעון's view. The חכמים say the house is impure because a ולד must be inside the שליא. רבי שמעון says the ולד dissolved before birth, so the house stays pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion assumes a real ולד is hidden in the שליא, so it makes the house impure. רבי שמעון agrees there was a ולד, but says it dissolved and was lost in the שליא. This matches the idea of ביטול ברוב in our lump of blood, as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
afterbirth, the sac holding the fetus
ritually impure
dissolved, melted away

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that a real ולד can lose its טומאה when it is lost in a bigger mass. This applies to the lump of blood (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב) and to the dissolved ולד in the שליא (רבי שמעון). It does not stop the birth from counting for בכורה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not deny that there was a ולד. He says it dissolved, so it no longer makes the house impure.

phrases.english: As we learned: If the afterbirth is in the house —
the house is impure.
Not because the afterbirth is an offspring,
but because there is no afterbirth without an offspring.
Rabbi Shimon says:
The offspring dissolved before it came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by quoting רבי שמעון's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון holds the ולד dissolved inside the שליא, so the house is not made impure.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the two תנאים share the same principle.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדה about a שליא in the house.

steps.title: A dead fetus gives טומאה only once its head is round like a skein
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a dead fetus does not give טומאה at the opening of the womb until its head is round like a פִּיקָּה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: Dead fetuses do not count as making 'the grave open' until their head is rounded like a skein of yarn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about when a dead fetus starts giving טומאה. This sets up the questions that follow about what 'like a skein' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once the womb opens, a dead fetus inside spreads טומאה. This משנה adds a limit: the fetus must have grown enough that its head is round and as big as a skein.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Fetuses born dead or not able to live
'Opening of the grave': here, the opening of the womb
A skein or ball of spun yarn

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a משנה in a different מסכת, in אהלות.

phrases.english: Dead fetuses do not have 'opening of the grave'
phrases.notes: 'The grave' here means the womb. A dead fetus inside it is like a body in a grave.

phrases.english: until they round the head like a skein.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about fetus טומאה, connected to the earlier discussion of a ולד inside a mass or a שליא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead fetus does not give טומאה at the opening of the womb until its head is round like a skein.

steps.title: What does 'like a skein' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of skein the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'like a skein'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about the measure in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skein can be made of many materials and come in many sizes. Without knowing which one is meant, the measure cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it?

phrases.english: What is 'like a skein'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which skein sets the size of the fetus's head.

steps.title: רב הונא: a skein of wool
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that it means a skein of woolen yarn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Like a skein of wool.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a first answer: the משנה means a skein of wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us the material, but not yet which kind of wool skein. That leaves room for the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
Like a skein of wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The skein is a skein of wool.

steps.title: חייא בר רב asks: a warp skein or a woof skein?
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב asks רב הונא to explain whether he means a skein of warp threads or of woof threads.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said to רב הונא: My teacher, explain: a skein of warp threads or of woof threads?
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks רב הונא to be more exact about which wool skein he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool for weaving is spun two ways: thin threads for the שְׁתִי and thicker threads for the עֵרֶב. A skein of each has a different size, so the answer changes the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Warp: the lengthwise threads on a loom, spun thinner
Woof: the crosswise threads, spun thicker
Explain!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: חייא בר רב said to רב הונא:
My teacher, explain:
Of warp or of woof?
phrases.notes: Warp threads run lengthwise on a loom and are thin; woof threads go across and are thicker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב הוּנָא רַבִּי פָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב הונא's answer by asking which type of wool skein.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the measure is a warp skein or a woof skein.

steps.title: A ברייתא: warp, woof, or a different sign
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says warp, רבי יהודה says woof, and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says it starts once טפיפיות are seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was taught in a ברייתא: A skein of warp; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Of woof. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says: From when טפיפיות are seen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers by showing that this exact question is a disagreement among תנאים in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר uses the smaller warp skein and רבי יהודה uses the bigger woof skein. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק does not measure the head at all; he uses a visible sign, טפיפיות, which the גמרא explains next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A visible sign at the womb, explained in the next step

phrases.english: He said to him: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: פִּיקָּה שֶׁל שְׁתִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: A skein of warp; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי יהודה says: Of woof.
רבי אליעזר son of רבי צדוק says:
From when טפיפיות are seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חייא בר רב's question by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a מחלוקת: רבי מאיר says warp, רבי יהודה says woof, and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says once טפיפיות are seen.

steps.title: What are טפיפיות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word טפיפיות means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are טפיפיות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain an unusual word in רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since his whole opinion depends on this sign, the גמרא needs to know what it looks like.

phrases.english: What are טפיפיות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the last opinion of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the sign called טפיפיות looks like.

steps.title: טפיפיות look like a mule bending to urinate
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, they explained in ירושלים that it looks like a mule crouching to urinate, with one round fold showing inside another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק: This is how they explained it in ירושלים: Like a female mule that bends down to urinate, and a skein is seen inside a skein.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a picture of what טפיפיות look like, passed down from רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a mule crouches, round folds of skin show around the opening, like one ring of yarn inside another. That ring-in-a-ring look at the womb is the sign that the fetus now gives טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A female mule
Bending down, crouching
A skein inside a skein: one round fold inside another

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that שמואל said
in the name of רבי אליעזר son of רבי צדוק:
This is how they would explain it in ירושלים:
Like a female mule that bends down to urinate,
and a skein is seen inside a skein.
phrases.notes: He means round folds of skin that look like one ring of yarn sitting inside another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טפיפיות are folds at the womb that look like a skein inside a skein, like a mule crouching to urinate.

steps.title: רב הונא heard two skein rules but cannot place them
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he heard of two skeins, one of warp and one of woof, but does not know what each one is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: I heard of two skeins, one of warp and one of woof, and I am not able to explain them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא admits that he got two skein measures as a tradition, but he does not know which case each one belongs to. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the ברייתא: both the warp and woof measures are real. But רב הונא does not know if they are two opinions in one מחלוקת or two rules for two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard, as a received tradition
I am not able to explain it

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
I heard of two skeins,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שְׁתִי וְאַחַת שֶׁל עֵרֶב,
phrases.english: one of warp and one of woof,
and I am not able to explain them.
phrases.notes: He knows the two sizes but not which case each one is meant for.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא שָׁמַעְתִּי שְׁתֵּי פִּיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a tradition of two skein sizes without knowing how they are used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditional skein measures, warp and woof, and their use is unknown to רב הונא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן heard three skein rules, including a large sack-makers' skein
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן heard of three skeins: warp, woof, and the large skein of sack makers, and he also could not explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: I heard of three skeins: one of warp, one of woof, and one of the large skein of sack makers, and I am not able to explain them.
steps.whatsHappening: A second tradition from ארץ ישראל adds a third skein size. רבי יוחנן also does not know where each one belongs, so the גמרא still needs an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three sizes instead of two. The new one, the large sack-makers' skein, is clearly a separate rule, so these are probably measures for different cases and not just one מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Sack makers

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said:
I heard of three skeins,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שְׁתִי וְאַחַת שֶׁל עֵרֶב
phrases.english: one of warp and one of woof

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת שֶׁל פִּיקָּה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁל סַקָּאִין,
phrases.english: and one of a large skein of sack makers,
and I am not able to explain them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב הונא's two skeins with a third, still without explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three traditional skein measures: warp, woof and the large sack-makers' skein.

steps.title: רבין explains: warp for a woman, woof for an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבין explains in רבי יוחנן's name that the warp skein is the measure for a woman's fetus and the woof skein is the measure for an animal's fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he explained it in the name of רבי יוחנן: For a woman, like a skein of warp; for an animal, like a skein of woof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין finally explains where the warp and woof measures belong: they are for two different kinds of fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sizes are not only two sides of a מחלוקת; each has its own case. A human fetus's head must reach the smaller warp-skein size, and an animal fetus's head must reach the bigger woof-skein size.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
An animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבין is just choosing between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. He is saying the two sizes are for two different cases: a woman and an animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since this מסכת deals with animal births, this tells us the measure for when an animal fetus starts giving טומאה.

phrases.english: When רבין came,
he explained it in the name of רבי יוחנן:
That of a woman is like that of warp,
phrases.notes: He means the head of a woman's fetus must be the size of a warp skein.

phrases.english: that of an animal is like that of woof.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין פֵּירְשַׁהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the warp and woof traditions that רב הונא and רבי יוחנן could not place.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warp skein is for a woman's fetus; the woof skein is for an animal's fetus.

steps.title: The large sack-makers' skein: the size of an impure clod of earth
steps.stepSummary: The third skein is the size needed for a clod of earth from a בית הפרס or from ארץ העמים to give טומאה. It is like the seal on large sacks or the top of a Bethlehem jug's stopper.
steps.simpleTranslation: The large skein of sack makers is as we learned: A clod of earth that comes from a בית הפרס or from ארץ העמים, its measure is like a large skein of sack makers, which is like the seal of large sacks, and that size is found on the top side of the stopper of a Bethlehem jug.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third skein from רבי יוחנן's list by showing the case where it is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This measure has nothing to do with a fetus. It is the size a clump of earth from a doubtful or foreign place must be to give טומאה. The גמרא gives two everyday objects of the same size so we can picture it.

keyTerms.meaning: A clod or lump of earth
A field where a grave was plowed up, so bones may be scattered
Lands outside ארץ ישראל, whose earth the חכמים made טמא
Large sacks
The stopper or seal on a jug

steps.whatToRemember: Three skein sizes: warp is for a woman's fetus, woof is for an animal's fetus, and the large sack-makers' skein is for an impure clod of earth.

phrases.english: The large skein of sack makers is as we learned:
A clod of earth that comes from a בית הפרס,
or from the land of the nations —
its measure is like a large skein of sack makers,
which is like the seal of large sacks,
and it is found on the top side
of the stopper of a Bethlehem jug.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבין's explanation by placing the third skein from רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The large sack-makers' skein is the measure for a clod of earth from a בית הפרס or ארץ העמים to give טומאה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three skein traditions are explained: warp for a woman, woof for an animal, and the large sack skein for an impure clod of earth.

steps.title: Brine from an unreliable seller can be purified by touching it to water
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting רבי יהודה נשיאה, rules that brine bought from an עם הארץ becomes טהור if it is brought into contact with מקוה water.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: Someone who buys fish brine from an עם הארץ should touch it to the water of a מקוה, and then it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling: brine bought from an עם הארץ can be made טהור simply by touching it to מקוה water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We worry that an עם הארץ, who is not careful about טומאה, made his brine impure. Normally you cannot dip a liquid in a מקוה the way you dip a utensil, so the method here is השקה: letting the brine touch the מקוה water. The next step explains why this is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Brine; the salty liquid that comes out of fish
A person who is not careful about טומאה and טהרה
He brings it into contact (השקה) with the water of a מקוה
A נשיא (leader), a grandson of רבי

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
One who buys brine from an am ha'aretz —
brings it into contact with water, and it is pure.
phrases.notes: "Water" here means the water of a מקוה. The brine just has to touch it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the discussion of skein measurements in steps 7-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brine bought from an עם הארץ becomes טהור through השקה with מקוה water.

steps.title: Why the brine is pure either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ruling with a 'whichever way you look at it' argument: if water is the majority, the touching purifies it; if brine is the majority, the bit of water is cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if most of it is water, once he touched it to the מקוה the water became pure. And if most of it is brine, brine cannot become impure at all. So what impurity is there? Only that small bit of water, and that small bit is cancelled out by the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind ריש לקיש's ruling by checking both possible make-ups of the brine mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine sold in the market is a mix of the fish's own liquid and added water. If water is the majority, השקה purifies the water, and the whole mix follows it. If brine is the majority, the brine itself cannot become טמא, and the small amount of possibly-impure water is cancelled (בטל) in the larger amount of brine.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it; both options lead to the same result
Touching a liquid to מקוה water in order to purify it
Able to become impure
Cancelled out by the majority

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling works in both cases: either the water gets purified by touching the מקוה, or the small amount of water disappears into the larger amount of brine.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if water is the majority —

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעָבֵיד לְהוּ הַשָּׁקָה טָהֲרִי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: once he did the contact for them, they became pure;
and if the majority is brine —

phrases.aramaic: צִיר לָא בַּר קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הוּא.
phrases.english: brine is not able to become impure.
What is there?
Because of that minority of water?
Those are cancelled out in the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the ruling in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In either mixture the brine ends up טהור: majority water is purified by השקה, and minority water is בטל in majority brine.

steps.title: The purification works only for dipping bread, not for cooking
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה limits the ruling: it helps only if the brine is used to dip bread, but not if it goes into a pot, because the cancelled water meets more water and 'wakes up'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: This was taught only for dipping bread into it. But for a cooking pot, no, because the cancelled water finds more of its own kind and comes back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה adds a limit to ריש לקיש's ruling, saying when it does and does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case where brine is the majority, the impure water was only cancelled because it was a small amount. If the brine is put into a pot with more water, the old water joins the new water and is no longer a minority, so its טומאה returns. For simply dipping bread, nothing new is added, so the ביטול stays.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this for... (a phrase that limits a ruling)
A cooking pot
A substance found more of its own kind
Woke up; came back to its earlier status

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is only talking about the case where most of the mix is brine. That is the case where impure water was 'cancelled', so that is the water that can 'wake up'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of ניעור, that something cancelled can come back. That idea is what אביי challenges in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לִטְבּוֹל בָּהֶן פִּיתּוֹ,
phrases.english: They taught this only for dipping his bread in it,
but for a pot — no,
since the kind found its own kind and woke up.
phrases.notes: The water in the brine meets the water in the pot, so it is no longer a small, cancelled amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of steps 18-19 to dipping bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The השקה method works only for dipping bread. In a cooking pot the cancelled water joins more water and its טומאה returns.

steps.title: אביי asks whether cancelled impurity can really come back
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי teaches רבי ירמיה's rule, and אביי challenges it: once טומאה has been cancelled, how can it come back?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי was sitting and teaching this ruling. אביי said to him: Can impurity that was cancelled come back and wake up?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי repeats רבי ירמיה's rule, and אביי attacks its main idea, that cancelled טומאה can return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's logic: once the water was cancelled by the majority, it should count as gone. Adding more water later should not bring back a status that no longer exists.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
But really...? (opens a challenge)
Impurity that was cancelled

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Dimi was sitting and saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: This is רבי ירמיה's rule about the pot from the step before.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But does impurity that was cancelled return and wake up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea of ניעור introduced in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's rule (taught by רב דימי) that cancelled water 'wakes up' in a pot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something that was cancelled should stay cancelled; adding more of its kind should not revive it.

steps.title: רב דימי begins a proof from a משנה about impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers אביי: don't you agree with this yourself? He starts to quote a משנה about a סאה of impure תרומה that fell into other produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said to him: And you, don't you hold this? But we learned in a משנה: A סאה of impure תרומה that fell...
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי pushes back and starts bringing a משנה to prove that cancelled things can come back. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי claims אביי should already accept ניעור, because a משנה shows it. The משנה is only begun here, so the actual proof is still being set up.

keyTerms.meaning: And you, don't you hold this?
But didn't we learn in a משנה
A measure of volume
Impure תרומה (the portion given to a כהן)

phrases.english: He said to him: And you, don't you hold this?
But didn't we learn:
A se'a of impure teruma that fell

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by starting a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That cancelled טומאה can come back (ניעור).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תרומות about a סאה of impure תרומה that fell into other produce. The quote continues on the next amud.
